title: Hayd, nifas and istihadah
intro: The rules for a woman’s monthly period, the bleeding after childbirth, and other bleeding.

learn.html: As girls grow up, their bodies change, and Islam gives clear and simple rules for this – just as it does for wudu and ghusl. Every Muslim should know them.

Hayd (the monthly period or cycle) is the monthly bleeding of a grown woman, which can last from three to ten days. A girl usually gets her first period between the ages of eleven and fifteen, depending on the climate, food, health and family genes.
The shortest time between two periods is 15 days, and there is no limit to the longest.

learn.title: Hadith
learn.html: The Prophet (SAW) said: “The shortest hayd is three days, and the longest is ten days.” (Tabarani)

During hayd a woman does not pray Salah and does not fast, and marital relations are not allowed. She does not have to make up the prayers she missed, but she must make up the days of fasting – best straight after Eid al-Fitr, or before the next Ramadan. When her period ends, she takes a ghusl.

Nifas is the bleeding a woman has right after giving birth. It can last up to 40 days – that is the longest time – and there is no limit to the shortest. The rules are the same as for hayd: no Salah, no fasting and no marital relations; the prayers are not made up, but the fasting days are – best straight after Eid al-Fitr, or before the next Ramadan.

learn.text: Istihadah – bleeding that is neither hayd nor nifas

learn.html: Istihadah is bleeding in a grown woman at a time that is neither hayd nor nifas. If it comes in the time of hayd, it is istihadah when it lasts less than three or more than ten days; after childbirth, when it lasts more than 40 days. A woman in istihadah is considered a sahib al-‘udhr (a person with a lasting excuse) and follows those rules – so she still prays and fasts.

learn.title: ⭐ Remember
learn.html: These are natural things Allah (SWT) created. If you have questions, you can always ask your mother, a trusted adult or your muallim(a) – there is no shame in learning your religion.
